access_note: Science Data Bank and DataCite list 72 public raster files under CC BY-SA 4.0. The files and drought-threshold implementation were not downloaded or checked numerically.
description: A Xinjiang Agricultural University team derived drought-characteristic rasters for Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and China’s Xinjiang region. The Science Data Bank deposit covers 1982 to 2020 at 0.05-degree resolution and lists 72 files under CC BY-SA 4.0. It starts with one- to twelve-month Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index series and identifies drought events using run theory. Grids describe event duration, severity, intensity and peak, plus annual frequency and mean-characteristic indicators. Water-supply, irrigation and food-system simulations can use them to define drought-exposure scenarios or compare simulated dry periods with an observed-index baseline. These are derived indices, not direct streamflow, reservoir storage or crop loss measurements. Event boundaries depend on the SPEI source and threshold choices, and grid averages cannot establish asset-level conditions. The files and threshold code were not downloaded, so individual raster orientation and missing-value conventions remain unverified. A related catalogue record provides global SPEI high-resolution drought indices; this deposit adds event-characteristic products for a narrower Central Asian region.
name: Integrated Dataset of Drought Characteristics in Central Asia (1982–2020)
